subject: Regional service impact: temporary routing alternatives and evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ops@brightlane.ai
Date: 2027-09-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Generation failures observed in APAC + EU — urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a surge of 502s and request timeouts from our storefront AI calls around 08:50 UTC. The errors appear concentrated in APAC but a subset of EU traffic also had elevated latencies and occasional timeouts. Impact: checkout personalization and search intent suggestions failing intermittently.

Can your team advise immediate mitigations (temporary endpoint reroute, regional failover, or other)? We also need logs for our audit — timestamps, request IDs, and whether tokens were dropped or retried. We are happy to open a quick bridge.

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform, Acme Retail
elena.torres@acme-retail.com

Attachments referenced: none (we'll attach logs if useful).

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-retail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-07T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Generation failures observed in APAC + EU — urgent

Elena — thanks for the quick report and the signal. We're on it. TL;DR: we can push a temporary traffic steering change for Acme that routes APAC traffic to our Singapore region (apac-sg-1) and re-route EU traffic to eu-west-2 while we remediate the underlying connector saturation. Below are immediate next steps we propose — please reply with GO if you want us to proceed now.

Immediate mitigation (recommended, 20–30 min):
- Step 1: Update your endpoint config to use regional hostnames (no code change):
  - production: api.redwood.ai -> ap-sg.api.redwood.ai (APAC)
  - fallback: api.redwood.ai -> eu-west-2.api.redwood.ai (EU)
- Step 2: Enable short TTL (60s) on DNS while we monitor.
- Step 3: If you use an internal proxy / CDN, add a header X-Redwood-Traffic: apac-fallback to force the regional route.
- Step 4: We'll warm model KV caches for your top 10 routes to avoid cold-penalty latencies.

We attached a small runbook (apac-reroute-instructions.pdf) with the exact DNS records and the change window. Also attaching a short checklist we will follow and the temporary monitoring dashboard link.

We will need:
- Your permission to apply temporary routing (we can also provide the commands if you prefer to execute).
- Slice of request IDs you observed (if you can forward a small CSV) so we can correlate.

If you'd like a bridge, Rishi and Laura are on standby.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-07T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Generation failures observed in APAC + EU — tactical plan

Kim/Laura — technical plan and caveats below. If Kimberly gets GO from Acme I'll run the changes and monitor metrics.

What happened (initial hypothesis):
- Connector pool saturation in apac-sg-1 region due to a sudden spike in long-lived streaming sessions.
- Autoscaler reacted but there was a 2–3 min lag where queuing increased and prefix cache thrash caused 502s for high-concurrency paths.

Tactical reroute steps I will perform (on GO):
1) Modify routing policy for Acme tenant via control plane: set preference apac-sg-1 -> eu-west-2 fallback.
2) Push a short-lived config: max_concurrency_per_host=80 for the affected service to limit burst head-of-line blocking.
3) Spin up warmed inference instances for model: openai-compat-xl-quant (warm top 20 prompts using synthetic traffic).
4) Enable prefix/KV cache retention 10x for Acme tenant for 1 hour.
5) Watch these metrics: 5xx-rate, p95 latency, queue depth. Rollback if 5xx > 1% or p95 > 1.5x baseline.

Caveats:
- Reroute will increase per-request egress latency for APAC by ~40–120ms depending on route. We'll annotate this in the customer message.
- If customer uses strict geo-latency SLAs, we need written approval.

Commands (example):
- controlplane set-route --tenant acme --from default --to apac-sg-1 --fallback eu-west-2 --ttl 60s
- controlplane set-policy --tenant acme --max-concurrency 80

I'll be ready to execute once we have customer GO.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 09:12 AM Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a surge of 502s and request timeouts from our storefront AI calls around 08:50 UTC. The errors appear concentrated in APAC but a subset of EU traffic also had elevated latencies and occasional timeouts.
>
> Can your team advise immediate mitigations (temporary endpoint reroute, regional failover, or other)? We also need logs for our audit — timestamps, request IDs, and whether tokens were dropped or retried.

Thanks for the details, Elena — we applied the temporary routing changes at 10:02 UTC (control plane) and pushed warmed instances for your primary model.

What we changed:
- APAC client traffic is now routed to apac-sg-1 (temporary).
- EU traffic is pinned to eu-west-2 for a 2-hour stability window.
- We increased KV retention for your tenant and warmed top 20 prompts.

What to expect:
- You may see a small latency increase for APAC (typical +60ms). Failure rate should drop quickly if the change is effective.
- We are collecting request IDs and a snapshot of request traces — attaching acme-traffic-snapshot-0907.csv (sample) and the runbook (apac-reroute-instructions.pdf).

Can you confirm:
1) Permission to keep the routing in place for up to 4 hours while we stabilize?
2) Whether you want us to proceed with a more persistent routing policy (30 days) while we complete the postmortem.

We have a 10-minute bridge available on request.

—Kim

> Thanks for the details, Elena — we applied the temporary routing changes at 10:02 UTC (control plane) and pushed warmed instances for your primary model.

Hi Kim — thanks for the quick action. We can confirm a big drop in checkout failures after ~10:10 UTC; conversions recovered on the majority of traffic. We still see elevated latency for some EU-originating customers (p95 ~ 480ms, baseline ~ 320ms).

Requests:
- Please share the full list of request IDs you captured for 08:45–10:30 UTC (so our SRE team can correlate logs).
- Please provide the temporary routing change record and the control-plane audit trail for compliance (we will need this for our SOC auditors).
- Can you share a first-pass postmortem (what happened, root cause hypothesis, short-term and long-term mitigations) by Friday?

Also, are there opt-in controls we can set (tenant-level routing policies) so we can self-toggle regional preference next time?

Appreciate the responsiveness — Elena

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-retail.com>, ops@brightlane.ai, Jacob Moreno <jacob@edgeproxy.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-10T16:45:00Z
Subject: Postmortem draft and next steps — apac connector saturation (for review)

Elena / Acme SREs — attached is a short postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-v1.md) and the change artifact for the temporary routing (control-plane audit link in the Drive folder). Summary below:

Summary:
- Incident: connector pool saturation in apac-sg-1 from a traffic pattern spike of long-lived streaming sessions, causing temporary request queueing and a ~2–3 minute window of elevated 5xxs for Acme tenant.
- Mitigation applied: temporary tenant-level routing change (apac -> apac-sg-1 fallback to eu-west-2), warmed KV caches, and increased concurrency soft-limits.

Action items (short-term):
- We will enable tenant-level routing controls in the console for Acme (opt-in) by Oct 1, 2027 (owner: Product).
- Improve autoscaler heuristics for streaming sessions (owner: Infra, ETA 2 weeks).
- Provide full audit trail and request IDs CSV (attached: acme-traffic-snapshot-0907.csv).

Action items (long-term):
- Add pre-warming hooks for high-concurrency streaming tenants (owner: Runtime, ETA 8 weeks).
- Add region affinity controls + UI toggle (owner: Console, ETA 6 weeks).

Please review the draft postmortem in Drive (link above) and let us know if any items should be prioritized differently. If this looks good, we'll schedule a formal postmortem review with your SREs and provide the control-plane audit records for your compliance team.

Thanks again for your patience — we view this as a high priority and will keep you updated on progress.

Best,
Kimberly Park
